WSVAflowR

Multi-model streamflow simulation for gauged basins, built for comparing models fairly and then driving them with a changed climate.

Give it a gauge, from USGS, Colorado DWR (CDSS) or your own csv, and WSVAflowR delineates the watershed, gathers GridMET climate and basin attributes from public datasets, and calibrates five process models on the same forcing and the same tests:

Model Snow Soil and runoff Routing
WBM + IHACRES degree-day, Jennings rain/snow threshold Thornthwaite-Mather bucket two linear stores + loss
CemaNeige-GR4J / GR5J / GR6J CemaNeige, elevation bands production store, groundwater exchange unit hydrograph + routing store (+ exponential store in GR6J)
HBV (TUWmodel) degree-day with snow correction, elevation bands soil moisture with nonlinear runoff upper / lower stores + triangular routing

Each model is tested on held-out water years (blocked cross-validation) and in a different climate (calibrate on wet years, test on dry ones, and so on), then calibrated on the full record so predict() can run it with any new forcing. Potential evapotranspiration is always computed from the meteorological variables (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith × land-cover crop coefficients), so historical and projected climate use one method.

library(WSVAflowR)
b <- wsva_basin_usgs("01154000")         # or wsva_basin(flow_cdss("CCACCRCO")), flow_from_csv(...)
b <- add_forcing(b)
b <- add_basin_attributes(b)
fits <- fit_models(b)
summary(fits)
plot(fits)
predict(fits, forcing = warmer_forcing)

Start with vignette("getting-started"), which runs on a bundled example basin without downloads.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mikejohnson51/climateR")   # GridMET access
remotes::install_github("KECognac/flowR")             # repository to be renamed WSVAflowR

The rain/snow threshold raster of Jennings et al. (2018) must be added by hand once (Dryad blocks scripted downloads): download jennings_et_al_2018_file4_temp50_raster.tif from https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.c9h35 and save it as inst/extdata/jennings2018_temp50.tif, or point options(wsva.jennings_path = ...) at your copy.
